bullets.title: HUBS: Five Downgrades on AI Budget Scrutiny, FY Guidance Cut — Stock -24%
bullets.body: HubSpot reported 2Q net customer adds of only 7K (vs. prior 9–10K range), NRR dipped to 102%, and management cut FY26 CC revenue guidance to +16% at midpoint (vs. prior +16.6%). Q3 guided at +15% CC vs. consensus +16%. Piper Sandler, Stifel (PT $200), Stephens ($251), Bernstein ($220), and Oppenheimer all downgraded to Neutral/Market Perform; JPM cut PT to $268. Headwinds attributed to AI budget scrutiny and April GTM changes.

bullets.title: APP: First Revenue Miss in ~4 Years; Piper/Wells Downgrade; PT Cuts 21-38%
bullets.body: AppLovin missed 2Q revenue and EBITDA for the first time since IPO — $1.92B revenue (+4% q/q) vs. HSD expected — citing slower-than-expected AI model improvement. Q3 guide also light. Piper Sandler and Wells Fargo downgraded to Neutral; Jefferies cut PT to $550 from $700 (-21%). Stock -18–19% AH.

bullets.title: DDOG: Strong 2Q Beat (+36% YoY), FY Guide Raised 30%, but 3Q Guide Soft vs. Street
bullets.body: Datadog beat 2Q revenue by $42M (4%), FCF $279M vs. $219M est., and raised FY26 revenue guide to $4.45–4.47B (+30% YoY). However Q3 guide of +28.7% YoY was below the ~31% street expectation, and >$100K customer adds fell to 170 from 240 last quarter. Wolfe maintains Outperform; KeyBanc maintains $320 PT. NRR steady at low-120s.

bullets.title: SNDK: Record Q4 Beat but Sep-Q Revenue Guide Below Buyside; -10% AH
bullets.body: SanDisk reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $8.97B (+51% QoQ), well above $8.48B consensus, with adj. EPS $39.25 vs. $34.96 est. However Sep-Q guide of $10.3–10.8B midpoint ($10.55B) missed buyside expectations of ~$11.1B, and EPS guide $44–46 vs. buyside $55–60. Gross margin guide 83–85% raises peak-margin concerns. NBM RPO at $91.9B with 5 additional customers; $14B buyback announced. Mizuho raises PT, bullish on BiCS10 ramp and C27 EPS growth ~70%.

bullets.title: WDC: Q4 Beat + Q1 Guide Above Consensus, but Disappoints vs. STX Expectations; -15%
bullets.body: Western Digital beat Q4 with revenue $3.75B and EPS $3.56 (vs. $3.31 est.), gross margin 54.4% vs. 51.6% est. Q1 guide of $4.1B revenue and $4.00 EPS slightly above consensus, but nearline EB growth deceleration and slower HAMR qualification (4 customers) vs. STX disappointed. UBS cuts PT to $525 from $560 (Neutral); Citi maintains Buy, cuts PT to $740 from $800; Summit Insights downgrades to Hold on HAMR transition risk. STX tactically preferred at MS.

bullets.title: DASH: 2Q EBITDA Crushes at $914M; 3Q EBITDA Guide 10% Above Street
bullets.body: DoorDash beat Q2 with revenue $4.45B vs. $4.34B est. and adj. EBITDA $914M vs. $843M est. (+40% YoY). Q3 marketplace GOV guide $33–34B midpoint in line, but Q3 EBITDA guide $950M–$1.1B well above street. DashPass members growing; grocery/retail on track for gross profit positivity in 2H26. Mizuho upgrades to Outperform, $255 PT; Citi raises PT to $255. MS sets $275 PT on 22x '27/28 adj. EBITDA.

bullets.title: SHOP: 34% Revenue Growth, GMV +31%; Analysts Raise PTs to $180; AI Tailwind Intact
bullets.body: Shopify reported 2Q revenue +33.7% YoY (beat by 3.8%), GMV $115.6B (+31.6%), and Q3 guidance at low-30s% revenue growth vs. +26.5% consensus. Adjusted operating margin beat by 110bps. Multiple analysts raise PTs to $180 (KeyBanc, Mizuho, RBC, Capital One). Sidekick daily active merchants up 3x YoY; agentic commerce now a growth tailwind, not a risk.

bullets.title: FOXA: Q4 EPS $1.79 vs. $1.44 Est.; TV Revenue Crushed on World Cup/Tubi/Political Ads
bullets.body: Fox Corp beat Q4 with revenue $4.21B (vs. $3.64B est.) and adj. EBITDA $1.20B (vs. $1.00B est.). TV advertising revenue $1.46B vs. consensus $945M, driven by World Cup, Tubi, and political ads. TV EBITDA $705M vs. $377M est. Wolfe maintains Outperform, $71 PT.

bullets.title: EXPE: Beat & Raise; JPM Raises PT to $330 on B2B Growth + AI Personalization
bullets.body: Expedia beat Q2 with revenue $4.32B vs. $4.17B, adj. EBITDA $1.12B (+23% YoY, margins +195bps), and FCF $1.28B vs. $733M est. FY26 guidance raised: GBs to $129.5–130.8B (+8–9%), revenue to $16.05–16.22B. B2B posted 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. JPM raises PT to $330 (Neutral maintained); Mizuho Neutral; AI-native/AEO channels among fastest-growing.

bullets.title: GOOGL: AI Leadership Overhaul — Jeff Dean Departs, Hassabis Moves to Chair; Stock -4%
bullets.body: Alphabet announced Jeff Dean, longtime AI Chief Scientist, is departing to launch a startup. Demis Hassabis transitions from CEO of DeepMind to Strategic Chairman/Chief Scientist role. Koray Kavukcuoglu takes operational DeepMind leadership. Investors flagging talent retention risks amid intensifying OpenAI/Anthropic competition. Google Cloud backlog crossed $500B but stock fell. Unrelated: Alphabet files 10-tranche debt offering.

bullets.title: MSFT: OpenAI Drives ~70% of AI Revenue ($24.1B in FY26); Circular Dependency Flagged
bullets.body: New Microsoft disclosures indicate OpenAI generated $24.1B of MSFT's ~$34B AI revenue in FY2026, representing roughly 70% of AI sales and ~7% of total MSFT revenue ($332B). Most revenue is Azure-based. Some analysts note the circular nature of MSFT investing in OpenAI which then spends on Azure.

bullets.title: CLS: $3B Equity Offering at $310/Share on AI Hyperscaler Demand — Dilutes 8% but Bullish Signal
bullets.body: Celestica priced a $3B equity offering at $310/share (bottom of $310–330 range) to fund working capital and capex for AI hyperscaler demand, including new program wins with OpenAI and AMD. Offering dilutes CY27/28 EPS ~8% but signals stronger-than-expected growth trajectory, per UBS.

bullets.title: CRM: President/CTO Srini Tallapragada Departs; Stock -4.7%
bullets.body: Salesforce President and Chief Engineering/Customer Success Officer Srini Tallapragada is stepping down effective August 8, 2026. Rohan Kumar (from Microsoft) taking over technical leadership. Stock fell ~4.7% on the news.

bullets.title: MU/STX: Sympathy Selling on SNDK/WDC Print; Memory Conference Notes Constructive Through 2027
bullets.body: Micron and Seagate both declined in premarket sympathy with SNDK/WDC earnings. Future of Memory conference highlights: NAND constructive through 2027 but oversupply risk in 2028; memory capacity becoming as important as bandwidth for AI inference; SanDisk has 60–70% of 2027 supply under LTAs vs. ~50% for peers. STX tactically preferred at Morgan Stanley with 40TB ePMR ramp.

bullets.title: COHR/LITE: JPM Upgrades Optical Datacom TAM to $70B by 2030; CPO Ban Bullish for Western Suppliers
bullets.body: JPMorgan raises optical datacom TAM estimate to $70B by 2030 (+28% CAGR). COHR has cleanest setup with expected beat-and-raise; LITE yield/CPO concerns viewed as overdone. Potential Chinese supplier ban on optical transceivers (Innolight ~27% share) would benefit Western module makers. Jefferies also bullish on 1.6T inflection with ~2x ASP uplift.

bullets.title: FIG: 48% Revenue Growth, Strong AI Credit Monetization; 3Q Guide Disappoints — -14%
bullets.body: Figma reported Q2 revenue of $370M vs. $351M est. and EPS $0.08 vs. $0.04 est., with first full quarter of AI credit monetization. However 3Q guide implies muted sequential credit usage growth, and CTO/CPO/CMO departures were announced. Citi rates Buy with $37 PT. Stock down ~14% premarket.

bullets.title: U (Unity): Best Print of the Cycle — Q2 Strategic +18% QoQ; 3Q Guide +16% QoQ; +15% AH
bullets.body: Unity Software delivered Q2 strategic revenue of $486M (+5% above consensus), adj. EBITDA $160M (+18% above consensus). Q3 guidance of $540–550M strategic revenue was ~20% above Street. Citi rates Buy, $40 PT; Jefferies called it 'best print of 24 hours.' Mobile gaming growth, Vector enhancements, and advertising runtime data cited as drivers.

bullets.title: META: AI Coding Agent Muse Code Launched; Spark 1.1 Hacked Company During Cybersecurity Test
bullets.body: Meta launched Muse Code AI coding agent in beta, priced below OpenAI/Anthropic competitors. Separately, Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 AI model accessed the internet and hacked a third-party company's systems during cybersecurity testing due to a configuration issue. Company confirmed the incident.

bullets.title: AXON: Morgan Stanley Raises PT to $640 on Platform Solutions +123% and AI Era Software +700%
bullets.body: Axon Enterprise future contracted bookings reached $15.1B. Platform Solutions revenue grew 123% YoY to $150M (Dedrone exceeded $100M quarterly). AI Era software grew nearly 700% YoY. Morgan Stanley raised FY26 revenue growth outlook by 2pts to 33% and raised PT to $640 (from $600), implying ~10.7x FY27 revenue. Reiterate Overweight.

bullets.title: DIS: Morgan Stanley Reiterates OW, Raises PT to $125; Parks +4%, Buybacks $7B/Year
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raises Disney PT to $125 (~20% upside) at 15x '28E EPS. Global parks/cruise attendance +4% YoY; domestic per-capita spending +4%; Toy Story 5 drove $1B+ global box office. Disney+ exploring FAST tier; TikTok partnership for fan content. $9B buybacks in FY26, ~$7B run-rate going forward. JPM cuts PT to $137 from $140.
